findings.evidence:
Confirm your order
then
Enter payment details
then
Choose a plan
findings.violation: The three step divs appear in the document in the order Confirm your order, Enter payment details, Choose a plan, but their order values 3, 2, 1 place them in the reverse visual sequence Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order, so the DOM order a screen reader linearizes no longer matches the sequence a sighted reader sees, reversing the actual decision sequence.
findings.fix: Reorder the three step divs in the markup itself to match the intended sequence, Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order, and remove the order declarations rather than relying on CSS to reorder them visually.

findings.location: Page level, header nav, lines 11 to 14, the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.evidence:
Plan a tripService alerts
; no search form, sitemap link, breadcrumb trail, or related-links list appears anywhere else in the document
findings.violation: The page exposes exactly one navigation mechanism, the two-link primary navigation menu, with no search form, no sitemap link, and no breadcrumb trail anywhere in the markup, and nothing in the page's own content marks it as one step in a linear process, so fewer than the two independent mechanisms the criterion requires are present.
findings.fix: Add a second independent way to reach this page, such as a breadcrumb trail showing its place in the site, a site search form, or a sitemap link, distinct from the primary navigation menu.

findings.location: Section 1 (Accessibility improvements), h2 and section body, lines 19 to 23
findings.evidence:
Accessibility improvements

followed by "Riders may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person." and "Passengers can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.violation: The heading reads Accessibility improvements, but neither paragraph beneath it discusses accessibility; both describe fare adjustments and real time arrival checks, and only the section's image, not its text, relates to accessibility, so a reader scanning this heading cannot predict that the section's actual text content covers fare adjustments and arrival information instead.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to describe the fare adjustment and arrival information the paragraphs actually cover, for example Fare adjustments and arrival updates, or move this section's paragraphs elsewhere and replace them with content describing the accessibility improvements the image depicts.

findings.location: Section 3 form, promo code field, lines 66 to 68
findings.violation: The promo code field is marked invalid with aria-invalid="true" and its adjacent error text reads only Error., which identifies neither which requirement the entered value failed nor what to change, and the error span carries no aria-describedby link from the input, so a reader has no way to determine what is wrong with the value they entered.
findings.fix: Replace Error. with text naming the specific problem, for example This promo code is not recognized, and add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" on the input so assistive technology announces the error text when the field receives focus.

findings.violation: The div's class name and trash-icon image indicate a delete control, but the element carries no role, no accessible name, and no keyboard affordance, no tabindex and no button semantics, and the image inside it is marked decorative with alt="", so nothing about this control is exposed to assistive technology at all.
findings.fix: Rebuild this control as a native button element with a visible or aria-label naming the action, for example Delete, or add role="button", a matching accessible name, and tabindex="0" with keyboard handling if it must remain a div.

findings.location: Section 3 form, Phone number label, line 64
findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label> against sibling labels <label for="topic" id="s3-form-topic-label">Route</label>, <label for="email" id="s3-form-email-label">Email address</label>, and <label for="promo" id="s3-form-promo-label">Promo code</label>, none of which carry a color declaration
findings.violation: The Phone number label is the only one of the form's four labels styled with a distinct text color, and no field in the form carries a required attribute, asterisk, or accompanying text explaining what the color difference marks, so whatever this label's color is meant to signal is conveyed by color alone, with no non-color signal a reader who cannot perceive color could use to recover the same information.
findings.fix: Remove the color styling if it carries no meaning, or, if it marks the field as required or otherwise different from its siblings, add a non-color signal such as an asterisk with accompanying text alongside the color.
